issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (UML and textual description) that orderMeal() should call to attempt serving queued orders. The solution implementation provides an equivalent public method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders(). This is a naming/signature mismatch between the specification and the reference solution and may confuse students about the expected method name/signature (especially if tests or graders expect checkOrderReady()).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the reference solution and the problem statement consistent. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Update the problem statement (or tests) if processOrders() is the intended name so students know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem text tells students to initialize both attributes (orders and stock) in the SealSaloon constructor (no-arg constructor). Later the statement explicitly requires that stock be static and that related methods be static. Initializing a static stock in an instance constructor contradicts the earlier instruction and may confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field initialized at declaration/static initializer.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify the problem statement: explicitly state that stock must be a static field (shared across instances) and note that it may be initialized at the point of declaration or in a static initializer. If the intent is to have an instance-level stock initialized in the constructor, remove the later requirement that stock be static. This removes ambiguity for students when implementing the class.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() (and instructs orderMeal() to call checkOrderReady()), but the solution implementation provides this behavior in a method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders() instead. This naming difference refers to the same conceptual operation (attempting to serve queued orders) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students when mapping the problem specification to the reference implementation or when comparing their own solution to the reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Align method names across artifacts. Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and keep orderMeal() calling checkOrderReady()), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(). This makes the solution match the problem specification and reduces student mapping confusion.
